construct: CYP17A1 deficiency impairs cortisol and sex-steroid synthesis. Elevated ACTH diverts steroid precursors toward mineralocorticoid-active 11-deoxycorticosterone and corticosterone, causing hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis while androgen deficiency causes absent or delayed sexual development.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Primary amenorrhea/sexual infantilism with hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis, low renin, low cortisol/sex steroids, and high ACTH identifies CYP17A1 deficiency with accumulation of mineralocorticoid-active 11-deoxycorticosterone.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: DHEA, androstenedione, and cortisol are reduced downstream products in CYP17A1 deficiency; 17-hydroxyprogesterone formation also depends on 17α-hydroxylase activity. 11-Deoxycorticosterone is the mineralocorticoid-active accumulating steroid that explains hypertension and hypokalemia.
